body:
Direct user question: "when I google 'ktappdev' the site isn't in the results."

ROOT CAUSE — not an indexing failure. A brand/signal mismatch. Diagnosis:

1. Site domain/brand = "Ken Taylor" (kentaylor.dev). On-page visible text, <title>, <h1>, <meta description> all say "Ken Taylor", never "ktappdev". Homepage H1 is `KEN TAYLOR` rendered as sr-only spans (letters animated, mostly aria-hidden).

2. Live page (verified curl https://kentaylor.dev/) contains "ktappdev" 22× but ONLY in low-relevance spots:
   - twitter:site / twitter:creator meta tags (Twitter card data, not used for normal SERP relevance much)
   - JSON-LD `alternateName: ["ktappdev"]` + `sameAs` github/x URLs (structured data, rarely drives the keyword relevance Google highlights for this query)
   - GitHub/X href links in nav/footer/body
   NOT in title, H1, description, or any visible body text. So Google has little on-page signal to rank this site for the literal query "ktappdev".

3. User's search intent "ktappdev" naturally returns github.com/ktappdev and x.com/ktappdev (their exact-handle profiles). Google won't swap those out for kentaylor.dev unless the site is topically relevant to "ktappdev" — which it currently isn't in visible text.

4. secondary: JSON-LD `identifier: "kentaylor"` (structured-data.ts:115,187) reinforces wrong identity; `SITE.author.alternateNames: ["ktappdev"]` (site.ts:15) exists but is NOT consumed anywhere except... actually alternateName IS emitted in Person schema at :114/:186. Fine. But identifier contradicts.

5. Bing DOES index kentaylor.dev (Bing site: shows results). Google block-me test inconclusive (curl blocked), but the more likely issue is ranking/relevance, not absence from the index. Site has been up with sitemap + robots allowing all AI bots; no google-site-verification meta in code, so unknown if Search Console is claimed — if never submitted sitemap, coverage could be sparse.

RECOMMENDED MINIMAL FIX (controllable in-repo) — make "ktappdev" a real on-page identity signal:
- Add "ktappdev" as a visible site identity string on the homepage (e.g. hero subtitle `/ktappdev` or footer copyright "ktappdev") so Google has on-page text relevance.
- Add `<meta name="keywords">` already supports it; pages can pass keywords. Homepage currently passes none (src/pages/index.astro:18 `<Layout jsonLd=...>` — no keywords prop).
- Fix `identifier: "kentaylor"` → `"ktappdev"` in structured-data.ts:115,187.
- Consider Organization schema / `@id` referencing ktappdev as brand, only if user confirms they want ktappdev as the brand (currently brand is "Ken Taylor" / kentaylor.dev).

NOTE the ranking caveat (ponytail): Google SERPs for an exact-handle query will almost always surface the exact-handle profiles (GitHub/X) over a .dev site named differently. In-repo edits raise the odds but cannot guarantee beating the owner profiles. The lazy high-leverage move is (a) add ktappdev to visible homepage text + title support, (b) verify Search Console.

USER ACTION OUTSIDE CODE (cannot be done in repo): claim kentaylor.dev in Google Search Console, submit sitemap-index.xml, request indexing. If still missing after on-page relevance + Search Console, nothing more of consequence in repo.

Question to resolve with user: do they want "ktappdev" to be the searchable brand identity of the site (then we make it visible on-page + fix identifier), or just "site not ranking at all" (then it's Search Console / content-relevance, partly external)?

No files modified (scout read-only). Ready for coordinator to dispatch builder on confirm.
